title: Empirical Failure‑Rate and Operational Impact Study of LLM‑driven NetOps Actions in Heterogeneous Simulated Networks (Provisional Preregistration, Adapter‑Aligned)
research_question: What are realistic failure rates and operational impacts (reachability loss, policy violation, rollback count, outage duration) of LLM‑driven configuration changes in heterogeneous, multi‑vendor simulated networks, and how much does a lightweight automated validator (with at most one deterministic LLM repair call) reduce those impacts?
confirmatory_hypotheses: H1: LLM‑generated configuration changes applied without automated validation cause operational failures (reachability loss or policy violation) in ≥20% of intents on the sampled heterogeneous simulated topologies.

H2: Applying a deterministic automated syntax/policy validator (with at most one LLM repair attempt when validator fails) prior to application reduces the operational failure proportion by ≥40% relative to Direct‑apply (target absolute reduction ≈10 percentage points under baseline assumptions).
H3: Outage‑duration distribution is right‑skewed with a heavy tail (median << mean), indicating rare high‑impact failures that dominate mean downtime.
H4: Automatic rollback occurrences are concentrated in changes that modify access‑control (ACL) and routing statements versus monitoring‑only changes (statistically detectable association).
exploratory_questions: E1: How do failure modes differ by vendor (VendorA, VendorB, VendorC) and by change type (ACL, routing, monitoring)?
E2: How sensitive are failure rates to validator coverage and to whether a single deterministic LLM repair call is required/not required (measured by validator pass/fail buckets)?
E3: How do simulated operator intervention‑latency heuristics affect measured outage durations?
benchmark_scope: Publicly redistributable sandboxed heterogeneous topologies (three distinct topologies assembled from public topology examples and public device images) executed in emulator replicas.
Intent→CLI tasks derived from a public/synthetic intent corpus assembled from license‑compatible public sources only (no private production traces).
primary_estimand: Paired difference in operational failure proportion per intent: P(failure | Direct‑apply) − P(failure | Guarded validator+optional single repair), measured across 400 paired intents.
secondary_estimands: Mean and median outage duration per failed intent by condition.
Rollback count per 100 intents by condition.
Vendor‑specific failure proportions and change‑type conditional failure proportions.
sampling_plan: 400 unique intents executed paired across two conditions on sandbox replicas; vendor/change‑type stratification as specified; randomized order within pairs; fixed RNG seed recorded.
power_and_precision_plan: Designed to detect ≈10 percentage‑point absolute reduction with >80% power (McNemar framework, α=0.05) under baseline assumptions; sensitivity analyses preplanned.
exclusion_rules: Pairwise exclusion for persistent infrastructure failures after retries.
Exclusion of contaminated intents flagged by exact/near‑duplicate detection.
missingness_plan: Automated retry up to 2 times; persistent failures exclude pairwise; sensitivity imputation reported.
analysis_plan: Primary: paired proportions with 95% bootstrap CIs and McNemar test; secondary: outage duration summaries, nonparametric tests, Kaplan–Meier plots; subgroup tests with BH FDR control; all scripts reproducible with fixed seeds.
multiplicity_plan: Single primary test; BH FDR (0.05) for secondary/subgroup tests; exploratory analyses labeled exploratory.
contamination_plan: See above contamination_plan object embedded earlier.
stopping_rule: Stop on completion of all 400 paired intents or upon triggers detailed in stopping_rule field above (in execution contract aligned document).
planned_outputs: Five‑page IEEE short paper including Disclosure Statement
